When it comes to hauling heavy or oversized cargo, two of the most commonly used trailers are flatbed trailers and lowboy trailers. At Rechtien International Trucks, we’ll explore what is a lowboy trailer, how it compares to a flatbed and the key factors that determine flatbed vs. lowboy load capacity.
What Is a Lowboy Trailer?

A lowboy trailer is a type of semi-trailer that sits much lower to the ground than a standard flatbed. It is designed for transporting tall, heavy equipment that would exceed legal height restrictions on a flatbed. These trailers typically have two drops in deck height—one right after the gooseneck and another before the wheels—allowing them to haul loads that are as tall as 12 feet or more. Key features of a lowboy trailer include:

items.label: Lower deck height for hauling taller loads
Gooseneck attachment for easy detachment and loading
Heavy-duty axles to accommodate massive weight
Ideal for transporting construction equipment like bulldozers, excavators, and cranes

props.text: Comparing Flatbed and Lowboy Trailers
Both flatbed trailers and lowboy trailers are essential for moving large cargo, but their design and applications vary significantly:
Flatbed Trailer

items.label: Deck Height:
items.desc: Higher than a lowboy, typically 5 feet from the ground

items.label: Load Capacity:
items.desc: Can haul up to 48,000 pounds but limited by height restrictions

items.label: Best for:
items.desc: Standard freight, including palletized goods, pipes, lumber, and construction materials

items.label: Loading Options:
items.desc: Cargo can be loaded from the sides, rear, or top

props.text: Lowboy Trailer

items.label: Deck Height:
items.desc: Much lower, around 18 inches to 2 feet off the ground

items.label: Load Capacity:
items.desc: Designed for extremely heavy equipment, typically handling up to 80,000 pounds or more

items.label: Best for:
items.desc: Hauling oversized loads that exceed height restrictions, such as heavy machinery and industrial equipment

items.label: Loading Options:
items.desc: Typically loaded from the front using a detachable gooseneck

props.text: Flatbed vs. Lowboy Load Capacity

One major factor when choosing between the two is flatbed vs. lowboy load capacity. While flatbeds are more versatile for everyday hauling, lowboys specialize in heavier, taller loads that require extra support:

items.label: Flatbed trailers can carry loads up to 48,000 pounds but are restricted by height limits (typically 8.5 feet).
Lowboy trailers can accommodate 80,000 pounds or more and allow for taller cargo (up to 12 feet).

props.text: Which Trailer Is Right for Your Load?

Use a flatbed trailer if you need to transport standard-sized cargo that can be easily loaded from the sides or top. However, use a lowboy trailer if you’re hauling oversized, heavy-duty equipment that exceeds height restrictions.
